notes.title: Use a mind-controlled spork in Psycutlery, a wild free platformer with lots of gimmicks
notes.content:
Here's a free game that you should try out. It's called Psycutlery, an action-platformer where you bring down an abomination of evil with a piece of silverware.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/09/use-a-mind-controlled-spork-in-psycutlery-a-wild-free-platformer-with-lots-of-gimmicks/

notes.title: Gimmicks are god in Psycutlery, a delightful free spork-driven platformer from the creator of Psycho Waluigi
notes.content:
The curse of plausibility and coherence lies heavy across this realism-centred artform. These days, you can't even give a platform character a woolly hat without first devising an in-game textile industry with appropriate supply chains, and a whole supporting cast of millworkers with names like Arthur Worsted and Jimmy Shuttlecock.

I prefer the disconnectedness of Psycutlery, in which you fight using a telekinetic spork, buy things with frogspawn, heal by eating toothpaste, and checkpoint progress by carving blocks of stone into statues of yourself, using the spork. The in-game reasoning for all this is basically "because developer Luke Tarlowe has the imagination of a Picasso and the attention span of a goldfish". Don't call it CRAZY. Call it refreshingly uninhibited and also, reminiscent of, Decap Attack and Ristar. Also, call it free.

notes.title: Psycutlery runs great on Steam Deck!
notes.content:
[p]This just might be the definitive way to play Psycutlery.[/p][p][/p][p]The game has been specially optimized to run as perfect as possible on Steam Deck, both at the default 60fps and 90fps (for OLED) settings.  Button icons are altered accordingly when playing on the system.  Runs at 720p (given the game's long development cycle, I hadn't thought to plan for 800, heh).  No keyboard input is needed.  It has been tested on Deck extensively, and in the process... I finally felt like I was playing my game for the first time, even after over a decade in development.

As someone who doesn't really game on (desktop) PC, I had originally wanted to publish Psycutlery to a certain handheld console.  Unfortunately, that goal was rendered unattainable when my attempts at trying to turn my deep passion into a commercial product proved stressful on a personal level.  Thus, I decided to make Psycutlery free - and console storefronts typically don't allow free games.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks to the Steam Deck, the dream doesn't have to die.[/p][p][/p][p]Psycutlery was specifically designed as a console game, and now it can finally be played the way it was meant to be played.  I'm so glad this device exists!  Here's hoping the game can get officially verified in the near future, but for now, I hope those of you able to do so will give it a try on Steam Deck.  And if you enjoy it, please tell your friends![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45688300/a50b17a2d893e4c129e09c75bf5cf9bbe588ad1a.png"][/img][/p]
